'''DecipherCon 2002''' was Decipher's third company convention, held 31 October–3 November 2002 at the Chesapeake Conference Center in Chesapeake, Virginia.<ref name="home">[https://web.archive.org/web/20021109040100/http://www.decipher.com/deciphercon/2002/index.html DecipherCon 2002], Decipher (Wayback 9 November 2002)</ref><ref name="loc">[https://web.archive.org/web/20020404113333/http://www.decipher.com/deciphercon/2002/info/conferencecenter.html The Chesapeake Conference Center], Decipher (Wayback 4 April 2002)</ref> Hundreds of players took part in over 100 tournaments, roleplaying adventures, and seminars.<ref name="home" /> It hosted the first [[Players Committee]] [[2002 World Championship|Star Wars CCG World Championship]]. [[Angelo Consoli]] defeated [[Greg Shaw]].<ref name="tfn">[https://www.theforce.net/ccg/story/World_Championship_Results_announced_64778.asp World Championship Results announced], theforce.net (3 November 2002)</ref><ref name="pc-sw">[https://web.archive.org/web/20021221153832/http://www.decipher.com/deciphercon/2002/reports/1103swyjjkresults.html Star Wars Players Committee 2002 World Championships], Kathy McCracken, Decipher Daily News (3 November 2002)</ref> The same weekend held the first [[The Lord of the Rings Trading Card Game|LOTR TCG]] World Championship. Mathieu Brochu defeated [[Alex Tennet]].<ref name="lotr-res">[https://web.archive.org/web/20021221153649/http://www.decipher.com/deciphercon/2002/reports/1103lotrresults.html The Lord of the Rings TCG Has Its First World Champion!], Kathy McCracken, Decipher Daily News (3 November 2002)</ref>

[[File:DecipherCon 2002 tournament hall.jpg|thumb|right|320px|Main tournament hall, 31 October 2002]]
[[File:DecipherCon 2002 Chesapeake Conference Center.jpg|thumb|right|320px|Chesapeake Conference Center, 2002]]

Decipher named the first twenty-one members of its Hall of Fame. ''The Two Towers'' expansion of the LOTR TCG premiered. ''Star Trek'' CCG Second Edition was demoed.<ref name="home" /><ref name="awards">[https://web.archive.org/web/20021221153541/http://www.decipher.com/deciphercon/2002/reports/1103awards.html DecipherCon 2002 Awards Ceremony], Kathy McCracken, Decipher Daily News (3 November 2002)</ref>

== Venue and dates ==

* '''Dates:''' 31 October–3 November 2002 (Thursday–Sunday)
* '''Site:''' Chesapeake Conference Center, 900 Greenbrier Circle, Chesapeake, Virginia 23320<ref name="loc" />
* '''Master of ceremonies:''' [[Mark Tuttle]]<ref name="open">[https://web.archive.org/web/20030220095305/http://www.decipher.com/deciphercon/2002/reports/1030openingceremony.html "Have fun ... that's what it's all about!"], Kathy McCracken, Decipher Daily News (31 October 2002)</ref>

The Conference Center is 12 miles from Norfolk International Airport. The main hall held over 150 gaming tables (over 600 seats). Other rooms ran design seminars, booster draft, and demos.<ref name="loc" /><ref name="d1">[https://web.archive.org/web/20021106034543/http://www.decipher.com/deciphercon/2002/reports/1031dayonewrapup.html And So It Begins: Day One Wrapup], Marcus Sheppard, Decipher Daily News (31 October 2002)</ref>

[[DecipherCon 2001]] was cancelled. For many players this was the first DecipherCon since [[DecipherCon 2000]] in Kissimmee.<ref name="d1" />

Tuttle opened the convention at 10:00 on 31 October in the Presidential Ballroom. [[Warren Holland]] spoke. A wall opened onto the Decipher store and a Chrysler PT Cruiser, the LOTR TCG champion's prize.<ref name="open" /><ref name="d1" />

== Star Wars CCG World Championship ==

Full results and lists are on [[2002 World Championship]]. The constructed pool was [[Premiere - Original VS3]]. The Players Committee ran the event. The purse was $10,000.<ref name="tfn" /><ref name="pc-sw" /><ref name="tfn-sched">[https://www.theforce.net/ccg/story/Star_Wars_CCG_Explodes_at_DecipherCon_2002_65230.asp Star Wars CCG Explodes at DecipherCon 2002], theforce.net (20 September 2002)</ref>

Two Day 1 heats ran Thursday 31 October and Friday 1 November at 2:00 PM: six games of Swiss constructed, top 20% to Day 2. Day 2 on Saturday 2 November started at 10:00 AM (six games of Swiss). The top 8 played single elimination from 6:00 PM. Pre-qualified Day 2 seats went to Regional, Open, and Mini-Open finishers and to returning champions [[Matt Sokol]] and [[Bastian Winkelhaus]].<ref name="tfn-sched" /><ref name="swsched">[https://web.archive.org/web/20021023190505/http://www.decipher.com/deciphercon/2002/events/eventschedule-otherccg.html Event schedule: Star Wars, Young Jedi, Jedi Knights], Decipher (Wayback 23 October 2002)</ref>

The final ended at 5:30 AM on Sunday 3 November. [[Jim Colson]] announced the places at the Sunday awards.<ref name="d4">[https://web.archive.org/web/20030220124438/http://www.decipher.com/deciphercon/2002/reports/1103dayfourwrapup.html Until Next Time: Day Four Wrapup], Marcus Sheppard, Decipher Daily News (3 November 2002)</ref><ref name="pc-sw" />

Consoli posted the Dark [[2002 World Championship Angelo Consoli DS|No Money, No Parts, No Deal!]] Watto 60 that won. Shaw posted Dark [[2002 World Championship Greg Shaw Force Lightning is TECH|Hunt Down And Destroy The Jedi]] and Light [[2002 World Championship Greg Shaw DCon2k2 Runner Up - LS|There Is Good In Him]]. [[Kyle Krueger]] posted a Day 1 Light Jedi Council Chamber list (''It's a Kyle deck''). [[Keith Watabayashi]] posted the Day 2 Light There Is Good In Him also played by [[Brad Reinhold]].<ref name="tfn" />

== Other games at the convention ==

The same weekend held World Championships for LOTR TCG, ''Star Trek'' CCG, Young Jedi, and Jedi Knights, plus an Austin Powers CCG championship.<ref name="home" /><ref name="awards" />

Mathieu Brochu (Canada) won the first LOTR TCG World Championship over [[Alex Tennet]] (United Kingdom) in a closed-room final shown on a hall projector. Brochu received $7,000, a Chrysler PT Cruiser, a One Ring replica, and a trip to DecipherCon 2003. Both finalists had qualified through Day 1. [[Marcin Solonczak]] finished 6th. [[Clint Hays]] finished 13th. [[Alan Sagan]] finished 14th. Day 2 had 95 players. Day 1's morning 1v1 constructed qualifier drew 194 players.<ref name="lotr-res" /><ref name="d3">[https://web.archive.org/web/20021221152138/http://www.decipher.com/deciphercon/2002/reports/1102daythreewrapup.html Tension and Endurance: Day Three Wrapup], Marcus Sheppard, Decipher Daily News (2 November 2002)</ref><ref name="d1" /><ref name="w2002">[https://wiki.lotrtcgpc.net/wiki/Worlds_2002 Worlds 2002], LOTR-TCG Wiki. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20260208104034/https://wiki.lotrtcgpc.net/wiki/Worlds_2002 Internet Archive]</ref>

Franklin Kenter won the ''Star Trek'' CCG World Championship over John Corbett. Kenter received $5,000, a trophy, a trip to Paramount Studios, and a trip to DecipherCon 2003. Day 3 Swiss ended Kenter 7 (+255), Corbett 6 (+251). Returning 2000 champion Eric Johnfauno finished 7th.<ref name="st-day3">[https://web.archive.org/web/20021106035232/http://www.decipher.com/deciphercon/2002/reports/1102stccgstandings.html Star Trek CCG World Championship Day Three], Kathy McCracken, Decipher Daily News (2 November 2002)</ref><ref name="awards" />

Jason Killby won Young Jedi ($500). Jeffrey Kahan won Jedi Knights ($500).<ref name="pc-sw" /> Geert Verhamme of the Netherlands won the Austin Powers CCG championship.<ref name="ap">[https://web.archive.org/web/20021221151938/http://www.decipher.com/deciphercon/2002/reports/1102apchampion.html Shagadelic Interview With the 2002 Austin Powers CCG World Champion!], Marcus Sheppard, Decipher Daily News (2 November 2002)</ref>

The Halloween party on 31 October awarded Heidi Farinholt (Trinity) first, Niki Rowland (Arwen) second, and Adelle Edwards (The Mummy) third. Bridget Gavin won best LOTR costume as Frodo. Matt Kirk won best ''Star Trek'' costume.<ref name="hallo">[https://web.archive.org/web/20021106034823/http://www.decipher.com/deciphercon/2002/reports/1031halloweenparty.html Starfleet and Wizards and Plates Full of Cookies], Kathy McCracken, Decipher Daily News (31 October 2002)</ref>

Decipher inducted twenty-one players, product champions, and retailers into a new Hall of Fame. Star Wars CCG names on that list include [[Bastian Winkelhaus]], [[Brian Hunter]], [[Joe Alread]], [[Jim Colson]], and [[Yannick Lapointe]].<ref name="hof">[https://web.archive.org/web/20021109035649/http://www.decipher.com/deciphercon/2002/reports/1103halloffame.html First Annual Decipher Hall of Fame Awards Announced], Decipher Daily News (3 November 2002)</ref>
